definitions.explanation: Indicates that something happened only a very short time ago.
Emphasizes the present moment, often stressing immediacy.

examples.japanese: たった{今|いま}{着|つ}いたところだ。
examples.english: I just got here right now.

examples.japanese: たった{今|いま}{電話|でんわ}があったよ。
examples.english: There was a phone call just now.

examples.japanese: たった{今|いま}{田中|たなか}さんが{帰|かえ}ったばかりなのに、もう{戻|もど}ってきた。
examples.english: Tanaka-san just left a moment ago, but he's already back.

examples.japanese: たった{今|いま}から{始|はじ}める。
たった{今|いま}、{大事|だいじ}なことを{思|おも}い{出|だ}した。
examples.english: Right this moment, I remembered something important.

examples.japanese: たった{今|いま}{決|き}めたんだけど、{来月|らいげつ}{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}すことにした。
examples.english: I just decided this very moment — I'm going to move next month.

notes:
An emphatic form of {今|いま}. The word たった adds emphasis meaning "just" or "only," making the time reference more immediate than {今|いま} alone. Very common in everyday conversation.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- たった{今|いま}〜たところだ: just did something right now
- たった{今|いま}〜たばかりだ: only just did something
- たった{今|いま}から: starting right now

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {今|いま}しがた: just now — slightly more formal
- さっき: a while ago — refers to a slightly more distant past than たった{今|いま}
- ちょうど{今|いま}: just now, right now — similar but less emphatic
